neighbours.label: inner word pieces of indigenous-language place and people names (Aboriginal, Native American, African), as opposed to English place names, the - pole's side of the distinction
fire: Our bus stopped at Coolangatta before reaching Mooloolaba.
The Potawatomi settled around Kalamazoo in that era.
Traders from Ouagadougou reached Mbandaka by river.
The Yindjibarndi people live near the Fortescue.
Missionaries reached the Shoshone camp at Pocatello.
She grew up in Goondiwindi beside the Macintyre.
The Kwakwaka'wakw carve masks on the northern coast.
The Mapungubwe kingdom flourished along the Limpopo.
quiet: Our bus stopped at Cheltenham before reaching Gloucester.
The Puritans settled around Plymouth in that era.
Traders from Liverpool reached Manchester by canal.
The Yorkshire people live near Harrogate.
Missionaries reached the Quaker camp at Lancaster.
She grew up in Southampton beside the docks.
The Cornish carve stones on the northern coast.
The Northumbria kingdom flourished along the Tyne.

notes: Card + pole: Puckapunyal, Murwillumbah, Michilimackinac, Imbangala. Card - pole: pieces of English-style names (Primrose, Bathurst, Montford). New names in probing fired the + pole, English names did not.
